result.title: Centralized Critics for N-Agent Ad Hoc Teamwork
result.summary: Centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) has become the dominant paradigm in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), motivating extensive study of what privileged information should be made available to the critic during training. While prior work has examined the role of global state in fully cooperative settings, the design of centralized critics for N-agent ad hoc teamwork - in which dynamically varying set of learning agents must coordinate with an arbitrary set of uncontrolled teammates drawn from an unknown distribution - remains poorly understood. We study this question by comparing two natural classes of advantage estimators: controlled history estimators, which condition only on the observation and action histories of the learner's own agents, and joint history estimators, which additionally condition on the histories of the uncontrolled teammates. We prove that both estimators are unbiased and characterize the conditions under which the joint history estimate attains strictly lower variance than its controlled counterpart. Empirically, joint history critics match or outperform controlled history critics across a range of NAHT tasks, yielding improved sample efficiency and final returns. Together, these results provide both a theoretical justification and an empirical recommendation for incorporating uncontrolled agent histories into centralized critics for N-agent ad hoc teamwork.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 N-agent ad hoc teamwork 中的集中式 critic 设计，比较仅依赖己方智能体历史的 controlled history 估计器与额外纳入不可控队友历史的 joint history 估计器，证明二者均无偏并刻画联合历史估计方差更低的条件，在多种 NAHT 任务上验证其样本效率与回报更优。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些信息应进入集中式 critic」的偏差—方差分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态应保留哪些视觉/队友证据、以及训练期特权信息监督的有效性提供概念类比，但仅为远领域启发，需核查。
